parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic جُلَاب (julāb), borrowed from Classical Persian گُلَاب (gulāb), from گل (gol, “rose”) + آب (âb, “water”). Doublet of گُلَاب (gulāb).

Borrowed from Arabic جَوَاهِر (jawāhir), plural of جَوْهَر (jawhar), itself in Classical Persian گوهر (gawhar); جواهر (javâher) has become singular in Persian and so has its own plural forms despite its etymology as a plural form.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِلْفِل (filfil), from Classical Persian پلپل (pilpil), from Sanskrit पिप्पलि (pippali, “long pepper”), ultimately from Dravidian.
